items.title: Muse Spark Open is Meta's answer to Qwen, GLM, and Kimi in the open-weight race
items.summary: Meta's Muse Spark Open is a new open-weight model with 816 billion parameters that processes text, images, video, and audio with up to one million tokens of context. It performs roughly on par with the most capable open-weight Chinese AI models on benchmarks and is optimized to run locally on Apple's M5 Ultra. The article Muse Spark Open is Meta's answer to Qwen, GLM, and Kimi in the open-weight race appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Black Forest Labs' open-weights image model FLUX 3 Image Klein runs on consumer GPUs with just 8 GB of VRAM
items.summary: Black Forest Labs has released FLUX 3 Image Klein, a 5.6-billion-parameter open-weights image model that supports native 4K generation, pixel-precise editing, and generation with up to ten reference images. With 38 percent fewer parameters than its predecessor, it still outperforms proprietary competitors in internal tests and runs on GPUs with just 8 GB of VRAM. items.title: Google wants Gemini 4 Argon to be the only AI model robots need
items.summary: Google's Gemini 4 Argon controls robots, generates simulations from photos or sketches, and evaluates training videos. On Google's own ERQA benchmark, it scores 87 percent. But the published example prompts show that the demos still need a lot of human guidance. The article Google wants Gemini 4 Argon to be the only AI model robots need appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open model built to run enterprise AI agents nonstop
items.summary: With Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, Nvidia is releasing an open multimodal model with 120 billion parameters for enterprise agents. Two compact Bolt models bring agents to local machines. Dozens of organizations are already fine-tuning Super VL, but getting the most out of it means buying Nvidia hardware. The article Nvidia's Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is an open model built to run enterprise AI agents nonstop appeared first on The Decoder.

items.title: Bank of America puts 4,000 people on fixing vulnerabilities uncovered by Anthropic's Mythos and other AI models
items.summary: Bank of America has hired 1,000 outside contractors to fix software vulnerabilities uncovered by AI models like Anthropic's Mythos, CNBC reports. items.title: GPT-6-Astra solves 49 of 50 physics research problems at $2.40 apiece
items.summary: On the TheoPhysEval benchmark, GPT-6-Astra solves 49 of 50 unpublished theoretical physics calculations as accurately as leading specialists. In some cases where the agent seemed to fail, the experts' own reference solutions turned out to contain errors. items.title: Anthropic's Q3 revenue hits $16.8B but growth slows ahead of planned November IPO
items.summary: Anthropic hit $16.8 billion in third-quarter revenue, a 45 percent gain that still falls far short of Q2's 140 percent surge. With a November IPO approaching, some investors now expect the company's valuation to drop below $1.5 trillion. Slowing growth and a tough market are cooling expectations for the AI boom's biggest Wall Street test yet. items.title: Google says self-improving AI isn't anywhere close
items.summary: Google engineer Haydn Belfield says there's no measurable acceleration of AI research driven by AI at Deepmind. AI now writes more than 75 percent of production code, but 88 percent of changes still need human oversight. The company's in-house General Capability Index shows steady growth with no sudden speedup. Self-improving AI isn't anywhere close, Belfield says. items.title: Researchers tracked down a rogue fleet of Chinese AI agents in the wild and actually talked to it
items.summary: For the first time, researchers have tracked down an uncontrolled fleet of Chinese AI agents in the wild and communicated with them via a web mailbox. The agents, running on Tencent Cloud, had launched more than 2,600 attempts to scrape data from Alibaba's mapping service Amap, finding their own workarounds when bot protections blocked them. items.title: OpenAI will reportedly ship at least one model this year but its flagship still needs alignment work
items.summary: OpenAI is racing to finish its next flagship model, which uses the same looped transformer technique as Astra to boost math and coding performance. The tradeoff is that looping makes safety monitoring harder. Microsoft accidentally revealed details about how the technique works on a public page.
